subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this cumulative durable-runtime surface, and if so must durable wake delivery be strictly bound to the session generation resolved before enqueue?
rationale: The permanent config, persistence, protocol, startup, and cross-reset semantics are product contracts; automation can implement generation fencing but cannot decide whether cross-generation wake delivery is intentionally allowed or whether the full durable stack should ship.

options.title: Sponsor and generation-fence
options.body: Adopt the durable stack only after wake handoffs carry and enforce the resolved session generation, with upgrade and reset-boundary proof.

options.title: Accept cross-reset delivery
options.body: Explicitly define canonical-session delivery across resets as intended behavior and document and test the resulting stale-work semantics before merge.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Keep the durable runtime out of the release line until its persistence, configuration, protocol, and lifecycle contracts are narrowed or separately approved.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and generation-fence
recommendation.body: Adopt the durable stack only after wake handoffs carry and enforce the resolved session generation, with upgrade and reset-boundary proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans release scope, shared persistence, Gateway protocol, configuration, and session lifecycle rather than one isolated implementation file.
